scenes.text: A sugar-cube-sized piece of a neutron star would weigh about one billion tons on Earth.
Neutron stars are the crushed cores left behind when giant stars explode.
They pack more mass than our Sun into a ball about twenty kilometers across.
That's roughly the size of a city.
Some of them spin hundreds of times every second.
Which is wilder: the weight, or the spin?

title: A sugar cube of this star weighs a billion tons 🌌
caption: According to NASA's Chandra X-ray Observatory, a sugar cube-sized piece of neutron star weighs about 1 billion tons. These collapsed star cores are only about 20 km wide! 🌌
